label: Q01
question: What licence applies to the sightings and effort data?
context: marmam-app's LICENSE (MIT) covers the app code, not the data; EDI knb-lter-cce.262 states its own intellectual-rights text. The release refuses license = unknown without this question open. Checked 2026-09-27: marmam-app's LICENSE is MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2024 PSTAT197-F23' (the UCSB data-science capstone that built the app), and grants rights over 'this software and associated documentation files'. The class did not collect the data, so it cannot license them; the lab must name the data licence. EDI knb-lter-cce.262.2 (read 2026-09-27 from the package zip) states those terms for 2005-2015; it is not a Creative Commons licence, so it is registered as 'custom', as for the other CCE-LTER EDI packages (euphausiids, phyllosoma).
proposed_answer: license = custom, the EDI knb-lter-cce.262.2 intellectual-rights text (scholarly use; acknowledge the originating investigator; no commercial use without written permission), license_url = its EDI metadata page. Please confirm it also covers the 2004 and 2016-2022 rows.

Hildebrand, 2017, ver 2).
proposed_answer: Cite EDI knb-lter-cce.262 (doi:10.6073/pasta/9ee6ca9b4a316708ca3d17ddc92debfb) now, and ask the lab to publish an EDI revision covering 2004-2022 (with effort) that the ingest can read instead of marmam-app.

label: Q04
question: Is DateTimeLocal Pacific clock time (PST in winter, PDT in summer)?
context: Needed to build datetime_start_utc; also used by the cruise track match. First render (2026-09-27): every sighting and effort start falls in daylight when read as Pacific clock time (05:00-19:00), so the times are local, not UTC. Whether daylight saving was applied looks cruise-dependent: on many DST-season surveys before 2015 effort starts about an hour before PDT sunrise, as it would if the clock stayed on PST. Checked 2026-09-27: EDI 262.2 has a 'GMT Diff' per row, and most cruises kept Pacific standard time (UTC-8) all year, even in summer; only CC0607, CC0707, CC1008, CC1207, CC1304 and CC1507 used PDT. Reading them all as America/Los_Angeles had put 1,529 sightings (and their effort) an hour early; the ingest now applies the recorded offsets (cruise_utc_offset.csv). The sunrise check agrees with EDI on 21 of 22 summer cruises and suggests CC1104 and CC1407 also ran on UTC-8, while 2016+ summer cruises look like PDT.
proposed_answer: Local Pacific clock time, converted with each cruise's own GMT offset where EDI 262.2 records it (41 cruises, 2005-2015: 35 at UTC-8, 6 at UTC-7), else America/Los_Angeles with daylight saving. Please confirm the offset for the cruises EDI does not cover (2004, CC1104, CC1407, 2016-2022).
